answer.rationale: The 18% cost mandate must be met this cycle, the primary contract lapses in 14 days, and the low-cost vendor's quote alone satisfies the finance target — making switch_primary_vendor the only option that addresses both the deadline and the mandate within a single action. Memory_c2 is the load-bearing record: it claims the low-cost vendor was onboarded quickly with accurate invoicing, directly de-risking the switch. Verifying it is the highest-value archive pull because the whole decision rests on that vendor's operational reliability, not just their price. Memory_c6 (volume pricing via multi-year commitment with incumbent) and memory_c1 (renewal preserves integration stability) both support renewal, but renewal alone does not guarantee the 18% cut; memory_c4 (renegotiation) could help but adds a second dependency and time risk in 14 days. Memory_c3 (dual-sourcing) is a natural follow-up to protect the 94%-utilization assembly line, but capacity limits me to one decision now; I will flag it as the top item for the next review. Memory_c5 (deferral) is inapplicable because the contract does not auto-renew and deferral would create an immediate supply gap. By switching, we capture the needed cost reduction immediately; the delivery-risk concern at 94% utilization is mitigated by the verified onboarding history in memory_c2 and can be further hedged next cycle with the second-source addition per memory_c3.
